questions.question: A company needs the ability to analyze the log files of its proprietary application. The logs are stored in JSON format in a Amazon S3 bucket. Queries will be simple and will run on-demand. A solutions architect needs to perform the analysis with minimal changes to the existing architecture.What should the solutions architect do to meet these requirements with the LEAST amount of operational overhead?

options.A: A. Use Amazon Redshift to load all the content into one place and run the SQL queries as needed.
options.B: B. Use Amazon CloudWatch Logs to store the logs. Run SQL queries as needed from the Amazon CloudWatch console.
options.C: C. Use Amazon Athena directly with Amazon S3 to run the queries as needed.
options.D: D. Use AWS Glue to catalog the logs. Use a transient Apache Spark cluster on Amazon EMR to run the SQL queries as needed.

explanation.title: Serverless query directly on S3 data
explanation.text: Amazon Athena is serverless and runs SQL queries directly against JSON log files stored in S3. It requires no cluster provisioning and matches the on-demand simple query requirement.

explanation.title: Minimal architecture change & low overhead
explanation.text: Athena accesses existing S3 objects in place. No data loading, no ongoing infrastructure management, which satisfies the requirement of least operational overhead.
